Sure, here is the translation of the ancient Greek text to English:

"Then Agamemnon, king of men, addressed him:
'185I am glad to hear your words, son of Laertes:
For you have handled everything in due measure and recounted it.
I am willing to swear to these things, and my heart urges me,
nor will I swear falsely by the gods. But let Achilles
remember here how he pressed upon Ares:
190and let all others also remember, that the gifts may come from the hut
and we may ratify the binding oaths.
But this I command and enjoin you personally:
Having chosen the noble young men of all the Achaeans,
to bring gifts from my ships, as many as we promised to Achilles,
195and to bring the women.
And let Talthybius swiftly go through the wide camp of the Achaeans
and prepare a boar to sacrifice to Zeus and Helios.'"

This translation aims to capture the essence and style of the original Greek text.
